factors: Critical distinction between compressed execution and retained model fidelity
Three Reader and one SharePlane editorial comparisons
complexity.rationale: The source makes consequential performance and model-quality claims with distinct evidentiary limits, requiring extended assessment.

sourceMap.rationale: Video introduces and qualifies the reported result. The corresponding article section and catalog claim remain explicitly unverified.
Video describes sparse activation, memory fit and custom code. The corresponding article section and catalog claim remain explicitly unverified.
Video distinguishes approximately 43–44 prefill, 9–10 decode and higher speculative peaks. The corresponding article section and catalog claim remain explicitly unverified.
Video questions quality retention at extreme compression. The corresponding article section and catalog claim remain explicitly unverified.
Video describes hardware and software caveats. The corresponding article section and catalog claim remain explicitly unverified.
Video examines hardware prerequisites and bandwidth. The corresponding article section and catalog claim remain explicitly unverified.
Video distinguishes demo from operational utility and smaller high-precision alternatives. The corresponding article section and catalog claim remain explicitly unverified.

sourceCoverage.rationale: Seven distinct video-cue locations map to seven claims and valid sections; the private caption aid was not independently authenticated.

supportingArgument.rationale: Source distinguishes developer-reported compressed model fit, MoE activation, measured rates and software dependencies from reliable intelligence.

evidenceRoles.rationale: The first-party model card supports architecture; video reports developer measurements; GhostMesh recommendation is original synthesis, not independent replication.

counterargument.rationale: A compressed model may produce fluent responses but degrade reasoning or coding; smaller higher-precision alternatives may outperform it.

tradeoffs.rationale: CPU memory fit may lower accelerator requirements but impose bandwidth, prefill latency, precision and maintenance tradeoffs.

falsifiability.rationale: Reproduce the configured system, compare matched representative tasks against higher-precision and smaller baselines, and record accuracy, latency and operational cost.

originalSynthesis.rationale: The decision separates fitting and executing the model from retaining sufficiently trustworthy intelligence for production work.

performance.rationale: Reported 43–44 prefill, 9–10 ordinary decode and speculative higher rates are distinct and unverified by independent benchmarks.

economics.rationale: A useful local-inference comparison must include memory, CPU/GPU latency, setup, maintenance and task-quality economics, not parameter count alone.

threatGovernance.rationale: No production adoption is warranted without workload evidence and source-independent validation; private fleet inventory remains excluded.

ownerDecision.approval: Tony explicitly approved publication of Reader #58 on November 13, then approved the narrow privacy-safe verdict amendment, source-first placement and citation corrections. Publication remains subject to valid independent review and exact-head CI.

gaps.rationale: Independent reviewer did not directly inspect the private caption aid or authenticate audio/timestamp alignment; custodian statement remains bounded.
Developer throughput and retained model fidelity were not independently reproduced; source-video publication day is unknown.
Independent review did not execute visual browser UAT, source-video playback, or production verification.

decisionRationale: After initial HOLD for private hardware disclosure, opening order and unsupported date assertions, the final article with seven timed links, source map and catalog received standalone exact-SHA independent ACCEPT. Limitations remain explicit; the recommendation is a controlled workload comparison, not model deployment.
